RSS headline: "Zelensky backs Trump's 'energy ceasefire' but says Russia continues to hit power plants"
JSON-LD headline: "Trump says Ukraine and Russia have agreed 'energy ceasefire'" (headline changed during the day)
By Tinshui Yeung, BBC News

Trump claimed Russia and Ukraine agreed an "energy ceasefire", "effective immediately", no details given. Moscow yet to comment.
Zelensky said it was "news" to him, then said Kyiv would support it if Moscow did:
"Ukraine is ready not to strike at Russian energy and we count on Russia's similar readiness and on the agreement of the president of the United States of America on this."
His officials "look forward to clear details of America's dialogue with Russia".

ZELENSKY SAYS RUSSIA STRUCK AFTER THE ANNOUNCEMENT:
Zelensky later said Russia hit a power plant in Kyiv with a drone, causing power cuts, followed by strikes on energy facilities in the north-eastern Kharkiv region.
"All of this happened after the president of the United States made his statement about an energy ceasefire."

UK: PM Andy Burnham said Britain "strongly supports President Trump's call today for a sustained energy ceasefire to start now". France, Canada and the EU also expressed support.
UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting told the BBC the UK did NOT support the diesel deal. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas echoed Zelensky's criticism on Saturday.
The BBC has asked the White House for further details. (No White House response reported.)

Seven senators (4 Republican, 3 Democrat) said the deal "runs directly counter" to a law banning Russian energy imports: "Congress was clear: the US should not import oil from Russia until it ends its aggression against Ukraine and ceases threats against our Nato Allies." Urged Trump to "reverse course".
Republican Senator Thom Tillis told NBC News the deal "absolutely will" put American lives at risk.

Saturday: Trump accused Zelensky of wanting to "make problems for the world", said it was "time for Ukraine to get a new president".
Zelensky pledged to hold elections (suspended under the Ukrainian constitution during wartime) if Russia agreed to a 60-day total ceasefire.
Six people killed in attacks on two Ukrainian cities on Sunday, regional officials said. One killed in Russia's Belgorod region; another man killed in a drone attack in Russian-occupied Donetsk.
Four-year-long war.
